title: Market Metrics That Matter: European Cash Equities
summary: European equity trading volumes lifted in October with trading activity shifting towards continuous trading sessions and away from closing auctions.
text:
Market Metrics That Matter: European Cash Equities
Welcome to the October edition of Market Metrics That Matter, your monthly briefing on European cash equities trends.
Don’t forget to visit Cboe Europe’s Market Share page for leading insights into European equity trading activity.
October 2026 Highlights
European equity trading volumes lifted in October with trading activity shifting towards continuous trading sessions and away from closing auctions
Total addressable activity (on- and off-exchange) stood at €81.1bn, up 4% on September 2025 and 6% year-on-year.
Total on-exchange average daily value traded (ADVT) reached €57.0bn, increasing 4.2% on September and 12% year-on-year.
On-exchange trading activity shifted away from Closing Auctions and towards Continuous Trading Mechanisms. Central Limit Order Books increased to 50.6% of on-exchange activity (from 48.8% in September), Periodic Auctions rose to 9.3% (from 9.1%), and Non-Displayed Order Books increased to 12.2% (from 10.2%), their highest share since July 2025. Closing Auctions accounted for -26.1% of on-exchange activity, compared with 29.9% in September.
Systematic Internaliser (SI) activity increased to represent 18.3% of total addressable volume, compared with 18.0% in September, and up from 16.4% in September 2025.
Paris-listed securities showed the strongest month-on-month gain in market share of the total market (+1.4%), while Zurich reduced the most (-0.8%).
Cboe Europe maintains strong position across key trading segments
Cboe Europe's overall market share increased to 23.6%, up from 21.8% in September. Market share gains were recorded across all major trading segments, including Central Limit Order Books, Non-Displayed Trading and Periodic Auctions, reflecting the strength of the platform's offering.
Cboe Periodic Auctions maintained its leadership position, capturing a 75.6% share of the segment, up from 74.3% in September
Cboe BIDS Europe, Cboe's block trading platform, remained the leading platform of its type for a 55 th consecutive month, achieving an above-LIS market share of 32.9%
Retail executions against Retail Liquidity Providers through Cboe's EBBO Retail Service reached €47.6m [DS1] ADVT, the service's fifth-highest monthly level since its launch in September 2025.
On 1 October, Cboe expanded its Additional Liquidity Provider Scheme (A-LPS) to include an additional 111 symbols drawn from the STOXX 600 and Cboe's large- and mid-cap indices. The programme provides enhanced rebates for participants posting the best bid or offer in qualifying sizes and is designed to improve top-of-book execution quality and deliver better outcomes for all market participants.
